verdict.rationale: Ente Auth has its own export path. The docs reference an "Ente's plaintext export format" and describe password-encrypted local backups, and the official CLI (Homebrew formula: 'decrypt the export from Ente Auth') can decrypt those exports. A community user confirms 'it otherwise lets you export/import your data,' while another notes you can't easily export into other apps' formats (e.g., Bitwarden/Aegis), which limits frictionless migration rather than contradicting that export exists. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party doc showing a one-step 'export all codes as plaintext' flow, direct export to other authenticators' formats, and hands-on confirmation of migrating out to another app.

support.subject: As a power user, I can export all my TOTP secrets in an open, readable format and leave for another app whenever I choose — no lock-in
